title: James's workshop (prologue)
logline: Archie brings you to James for pearls; the calc notices you, Archie leaves, and James makes you his stand-in pearl maker.
questions: Board rebuilt from the event's existing art for the art-judge agreement run. Each shot's takes are the matching assets/reference-plates/james_meeting_* draft plus older versions from assets/events/ copied in as _vN.
Text says 'storage unit'; the placed exterior is a green door between shopfronts. The older card1/card2 art shows a roller-shutter unit (#34). Briefs follow the placed art.

cards.text: The storage unit 2 doors down from the halal supermarket. Archie is already there, which has never happened before. He used his last pearl in Whitechapel, and since then he checks the street every time a car slows.
cards.why: Card 1 can't start blank: James's door on a wet Bermondsey night, Archie already waiting.

cards.speaker: Archie
cards.text: "James makes pearls. I need pearls. Next time someone gets a knife out, I'd like more than a carrier bag to wave at them. So be polite, touch nothing, and let me do the talking."
cards.why: Archie's line; the street keeps moving past him.

cards.text: The door opens. James is in his sixties: glasses with one bent arm, a waistcoat with the slightest stain on it. He looks at Archie, then at you, like a parcel left on the wrong doorstep.
cards.why: The door opens: first sight of James.

cards.speaker: James
cards.text: "You're early. That's new. Come in. Touch nothing."
cards.why: James's line in the same doorway.

cards.text: Shelves of jars run to the ceiling, each labelled in biro. It smells of copper and bleach. Archie stays by the door and rubs his eyes.
cards.why: Inside: the workshop, Archie by the door rubbing his eyes.

cards.text: You pass a jar marked TIME. The calc inside shifts. It moves to the side of the glass nearest your hand, as if it noticed you.
cards.why: The jar moment is in the text; the room already shows the jars.

cards.text: You glance up. James is watching you. His expression doesn't change, exactly. But something in it does.
cards.why: James's look at you is the beat.

cards.speaker: Archie
cards.text: "James is the best craftsman I know. Everything I carry is his."
cards.why: Archie and James talk business.

cards.speaker: James
cards.text: "I'm the only craftsman you know. There's a difference." He turns to Archie. "Forty units of life calc, collected from Stratford within the hour. Do it and your next batch of pearls is at cost."
cards.why: Same two-shot.

cards.speaker: Archie
cards.text: "Who's the seller? Anyone I need to worry about?"
cards.why: Same two-shot.

cards.speaker: James
cards.text: "Nobody who's ever shortchanged me. The address will be on your phone by the time you reach the station." He doesn't look at you. "I need your friend's assistance with something in the meantime."
cards.why: Same two-shot.

cards.speaker: Archie
cards.text: He looks at you, not James. "Your call. Stay here, or come to Stratford and carry a bag."
cards.why: Archie turns to you: your call.

cards.speaker: You
cards.text: You think about the pearl that stopped the knife, and about rent. "I'll stay."
cards.why: You stay; Archie has gone. James alone.

cards.speaker: Archie
cards.text: "Lovely. Ring me if he's more horrible than usual." He's gone before James can answer.
cards.why: Archie's exit line is said leaving; the room is already his absence.

cards.speaker: James
cards.text: He takes down the jar marked TIME and sets it on the bench. "My assistant is indisposed and I have an order for time pearls. You'll do. Gloves." Inside the jar, the calc drifts to the side nearest you again. James is looking at the jar, not at you.
cards.why: James takes down the TIME jar.

cards.speaker: James
cards.text: "That hourglass Archie broke in Mile End. That was one of mine." He says it to the jar. "It did what it was made for. Now you."
cards.why: Spoken to the jar.

cards.speaker: James
cards.text: "I assume you've never made one." You haven't. "Then I'll explain it once. A pearl that seals is worth a hundred and twenty pounds to someone frightened. A pearl that doesn't is my calc on the floor. Do try not to fuck it up."
cards.why: Same.

cards.speaker: James
cards.text: He measures out the calc. "Plato wrote about orichalchum in the Critias. Second only to gold, in Atlantis." He glances at you. "You have no idea what the Critias is, do you."
cards.why: James measures out the calc at the bench.

cards.speaker: James
cards.text: You don't answer. "Two and a half thousand years ago, people knew exactly what this was worth. Today Archie is collecting it outside a Poundland in Stratford. Make of that what you will about humanity."
cards.why: Same.

cards.text: James sets a glass sphere in front of you and a measure of his own calc beside it. "My calc, so you can stop counting it. Press, then heat. Don't leave until it seals."
cards.why: The crafting choice plays over the bench.

cards.text: James wipes the bench down, caps the jar and puts it back on its shelf. Then he places a battered crafting kit on the table.
cards.why: Two hours later: bench wiped, the kit on the table.

cards.speaker: James
cards.text: "The kit is payment, along with a sample of the pearls you made today." A pause. "Keep practising and you may yet make more than a living out of this."
cards.why: Payment and the exit.

plates.name: james_exterior
plates.camera: Across the wet pavement, eye level, square on to James's green door between two shopfronts
plates.prompt: A blank background plate for a pixel-art game scene: James's green front door in Bermondsey, South London, set back in a short brick passage between two small shopfronts with awnings, potted plants and a pendant lamp over the door. Night after rain: the paved pavement in the foreground is wet and reflects the shop lights. Camera: standing eye height, square on to the door, the door centred in the upper half. No people. No text unless vital to the scene. Portrait 2:3 (1024x1536).

plates.name: james_workshop
plates.camera: From just inside the door, eye level, down the narrow workshop: shelves of jars and books ahead, bench on the right
plates.prompt: A blank background plate for a pixel-art game scene: James's cramped workshop inside a Bermondsey storage unit. Bookshelves and shelves of labelled glass jars to the ceiling at the back, a long wooden workbench with brass instruments, green-shaded lamps and stacked books on the right, a stool, a chair and pot plants on the left, a red patterned runner rug down the middle. Warm lamplight. Camera: standing eye height just inside the door, looking down the room. No people. No text unless vital to the scene. Portrait.
